title_en: On the Unity of the Catholic Church
author: Cyprian of Carthage
addressee: The faithful brethren (fratres dilectissimi), especially the bishops who preside in the Church
occasion: Cyprian writes to warn the faithful against schism and heresy, which he sees as a subtler and more dangerous attack by the devil than open persecution, and to defend the unity of the Church against those who have broken away from it.
argument: Cyprian argues that the Church is one and indivisible, founded by Christ upon Peter as the single source of its unity, and that this unity is preserved through the one episcopate. He warns that schismatics and heretics, though they may claim the name of Christian and even suffer death, are cut off from the Church and cannot be saved. He urges the faithful to separate from those who have broken unity, while exhorting the loyal to hold fast to peace, love, and the commandments of Christ.

outline.move: Cyprian warns that the devil's hidden attacks through deception are more dangerous than open persecution, and urges obedience to Christ's commandments as the path to immortality.
He identifies heresies and schisms as the devil's new fraud, by which he deceives people under the very title of Christian.
He grounds the Church's unity in Christ's words to Peter and in the one, indivisible episcopate, illustrated by the images of the sun's rays, tree branches, and streams from one fountain.
He insists that no one outside the Church can have God as Father, and uses the seamless tunic of Christ and the one house of the Passover to show that the Church cannot be divided.
He presents the dove as the model of the Church's simplicity and charity, and contrasts it with the ferocity of those who have separated.
He explains that heresies arise from discordant minds and are permitted by God to test the faithful, and he denounces false teachers who promise salvation apart from the one baptism.
He refutes the misuse of Christ's saying about two or three gathered in his name, showing that it applies to the unanimous within the Church, not to those separated from it.
He teaches that peace with brethren is required for prayer and sacrifice, and that even martyrdom cannot profit those who lack love and remain outside the Church.
He describes the growth of schismatic wickedness in the last days as foretold by the Apostle, and urges the faithful to avoid those who have separated.
He cites the punishments of Korah, Dathan, Abiram, King Uzziah, and Aaron's sons as warnings against those who rebel against God's appointed order.

He warns that even confessors can fall after their confession, that perseverance wins the crown, and that the fall of some does not destroy the dignity of the whole body of confessors, just as Judas's betrayal did not destroy the apostles' faith.
He urges the faithful to separate from schismatics and to pursue peace, since the Church is one body that cannot be divided.
He contrasts the unanimity of the apostolic Church with the present decline of faith, and exhorts the brethren to wakefulness and readiness for the Lord's coming.

cast.name: Cyprian
cast.who: Bishop of Carthage and author of the treatise.

cast.name: Peter
cast.who: The apostle upon whom Christ founded the Church and from whom its unity begins.

cast.name: Paul
cast.who: The apostle whose letters Cyprian cites on unity, love, and the last days.

cast.name: John
cast.who: The apostle and evangelist cited on those who went out from the Church and on God as love.

cast.name: Korah
cast.who: Rebel against Moses and Aaron, punished by the earth opening and fire from the Lord.

cast.name: Dathan
cast.who: Rebel against Moses and Aaron, punished with Korah.

cast.name: Abiram
cast.who: Rebel against Moses and Aaron, punished with Korah.

cast.name: Uzziah
cast.who: King who unlawfully took up the censer and was struck with leprosy.

cast.name: Aaron
cast.who: The priest; his sons were destroyed for offering strange fire.

cast.name: Ahijah
cast.who: The prophet who tore his garment to signify the division of Solomon's kingdom.

cast.name: Rahab
cast.who: The woman in whose house the Church was prefigured.

cast.name: Solomon
cast.who: King whose kingdom was divided after his death.

cast.name: Judas
cast.who: The apostle who betrayed the Lord, showing that even the chosen can fall.

cast.name: Jannes
cast.who: One of the magicians who resisted Moses, cited by Paul as a type of false teachers.

cast.name: Jambres
cast.who: One of the magicians who resisted Moses, cited by Paul as a type of false teachers.

voices.speaker: The Lord (Christ)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by phrases such as 'loquitur Dominus ad Petrum', 'monet Dominus et dicit', 'dicit Dominus', or by direct quotation from the Gospels.

voices.speaker: Paul the Apostle
voices.how_marked: Introduced by phrases such as 'apostolus Paulus ... dicens', 'per apostolum praemonet Spiritus sanctus', or 'beatus apostolus loquitur'. In section 16 the attribution is joint: 'praenuntiante per apostolum nobis et praemonente Spiritu sancto'.

voices.speaker: John the Apostle
voices.how_marked: Introduced by phrases such as 'Iohannes apostolus dicens' or 'Iohannis beati apostoli uox est'.

voices.speaker: The Holy Spirit
voices.how_marked: Introduced by phrases such as 'Spiritus sanctus ... designat et dicit' or 'Spiritus sanctus in psalmis dicens'. In section 16 the Holy Spirit speaks through Paul: 'praenuntiante per apostolum nobis et praemonente Spiritu sancto'.

voices.speaker: Scripture (divina scriptura)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by phrases such as 'loquitur ac dicit scriptura diuina' or 'probat scriptura quae dicit'.

key_terms.sense: The oneness of the Church, grounded in its single origin from Peter and preserved in the one episcopate; the central theme of the work.
The one Catholic Church, the bride of Christ and mother of the faithful, outside of which there is no salvation.
The office of bishop, which is one and undivided, held in solidum by individual bishops.
Divisions or splits in the Church, created by those who break away from its unity.
False teachings and factions invented by the devil to subvert faith and corrupt truth.
The harmony and agreement among the faithful that preserves the bond of unity.
The peace of Christ, which schismatics break and which the faithful must preserve.
The love that binds the brethren together; without it, even martyrdom profits nothing.
One who suffers death for confessing Christ; Cyprian insists that no one outside the Church can be a true martyr.
One who has confessed Christ under persecution but has not yet been put to death; confession is only the beginning of glory.
The seamless tunic of Christ, a symbol of the Church's indivisible unity.
The dove, symbol of the Holy Spirit and of the simplicity, peace, and unanimity that should characterize the Church.
A sacred sign or mystery that reveals and embodies the Church's unity, such as the seamless tunic or the Passover lamb.
The one baptism of the Church; those who baptize outside the Church offer no true cleansing.
The altar of the Church, against which schismatics rebel by setting up another altar.

scripture: Cyprian quotes from the Old Latin version of the Bible, which generally follows the Septuagint (LXX) for the Old Testament. Psalm numbering follows the LXX/Vulgate tradition. In modern citation, LXX Psalm numbers should be converted to the Hebrew/English numbering where they differ (e.g., LXX Psalm 9 is English Psalms 9-10; LXX Psalms 10-112 are one number higher in English). Book names should be given in their modern English forms (e.g., 'the first of Kingdoms' as 1 Samuel, 'Jesus son of Nave' as Joshua, 'Exodus' as Exodus, 'Canticle of Canticles' as Song of Songs). New Testament quotations should be cited by modern book, chapter, and verse.
uncertain: The precise date of composition is not stated in the text; 251 AD is the commonly accepted date based on external evidence, but the text itself does not specify it.
The exact identity of the schismatics Cyprian opposes is not named in the text; they are referred to generally as schismatics, heretics, false prophets, and those who set up rival altars.
The precise biblical text form (Old Latin version) behind each quotation cannot be fully reconstructed from the source alone.

_unresolved_facts.claim: especially the bishops who preside in the Church
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Cauenda sunt autem non solum quae sunt aperta adque manifesta sed et astutae fraudis subtilitate fallentia... Hoc eo fit, fratres dilectissimi, dum ad ueritatis originem non reditur nec caput quaeritur nec magisterii caelestis doctrina seruatur.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cyprian writes to warn the faithful brethren (fratres dilectissimi) against schism and heresy; the special address to bishops in section 5 is a secondary emphasis within the broader exhortation to all the faithful, not the primary addressee of the treatise as a whole.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Aaron: The priest; his sons were destroyed for offering strange fire.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: et filii Aaron, qui inposuerunt altari ignem alienum quem non praeceperat Dominus, in conspectu statim Domini uindicantis extincti sunt.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Aaron: The high priest; his sons Nadab and Abihu (not named by Cyprian) were destroyed for offering strange fire.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: inmortalitatem autem potiri quomodo possumus, nisi ea quibus mors expugnatur et uincitur Christi mandata seruemus ipso monente et dicente: si uis ad uitam uenire, serua mandata
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Lord (Christ): sections ["2", "4", "6", "8", "11", "12", "13", "14", "15", "17", "19", "21", "24", "26", "27"] — Section 1 contains no words of Christ; it contains Cyprian's own warning about the devil's deception, with references to Genesis 3 and the temptation of Christ, but no direct quotation of Christ.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: quando et beatus apostolus Paulus hoc idem doceat et sacramentum unitatis ostendat dicens: unum corpus et unus spiritus, una spes uocationis uestrae, unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma, unus Deus.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Paul the Apostle: sections ["4", "8", "10", "14", "16", "22", "23"] — Section 4 contains Paul's words, but the brief's note about section 16's joint attribution is inaccurate: in section 16, Paul is the speaker, with the Holy Spirit speaking through him ('praenuntiante per apostolum nobis et praemonente Spiritu sancto'), not a joint attribution of two distinct speakers.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: quam unam ecclesiam etiam in cantico canticorum Spiritus sanctus ex persona Domini designat et dicit: una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genetrici suae.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Holy Spirit: sections ["4", "10", "16", "24"] — In section 4, the Holy Spirit speaks 'ex persona Domini' (in the person of the Lord), which is a distinct mode of speech; the brief should note this special case. Additionally, section 4 contains two Holy Spirit quotations (Song of Songs and Ephesians via Paul), not one.

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["20", "21", "22"]: He warns that even confessors can fall after their confession, that perseverance wins the crown, and that the fall of some does not destroy the dignity of the whole body of confessors, just as Judas's betrayal did not destroy the apostles' faith.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Nam et Iudam inter apostolos Dominus elegit, et tamen Dominum Iudas postmodum tradidit. non tamen idcirco apostolorum firmitas et fides cecidit, quia proditor Iudas ab eorum societate defecit. sic et hic non statim confessorum sanctitas et dignitas comminuta est, quia quorundam fides fracta est.
_unresolved_facts.fix: sections ["20", "21", "22"]: He warns that even confessors can fall after their confession (20-21), that perseverance wins the crown (21), and that the fall of some does not destroy the dignity of the whole body of confessors, just as Judas's betrayal did not destroy the apostles' faith (22). Note: The Judas comparison applies specifically to confessors, not to apostles as a general category—the analogy is 'sic et hic' (so also here), comparing Judas among apostles to fallen confessors among confessors.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: si potuit euadere quisque extra arcam Noe fuit, et qui extra ecclesiam foris fuerit euadit.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Noah appears in the source text (section 6), so this name entry is correct, but the brief's 'names' section should indicate that 'Noe' appears in section 6, not leave it as an unlocated entry.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: quia nec ad Cain munera respexit Deus: neque enim habere pacatum Deum poterat qui cum fratre pacem per zeli discordiam non habebat.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Cain appears in the source text (section 13), so this name entry is correct, but the brief's 'names' section should indicate that 'Cain' appears in section 13, not leave it as an unlocated entry.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: et duo sceptra erunt ei propter seruum meum Dauid et propter Hierusalem ciuitatem quam elegi, ut ponam nomen meum illic.
_unresolved_facts.fix: David appears in the source text (section 7), so this name entry is correct, but the brief's 'names' section should indicate that 'Dauid' appears in section 7, not leave it as an unlocated entry.
